espinosa--laranja-reserva.description: Espinosa's La Zona factory in Estelí rolls this line, shown at the 2014 trade show, in a rare Brazilian leaf called Laranja over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It smokes creamy and smooth, with a bright citrus tang and soft spice running through a long, unhurried evening smoke.

thirds.notes: A light spice and a tangy citrus note open the smoke, with hints of cocoa and something floral behind them.
The smoke turns creamier and sweeter; the citrus lingers while cedar, vanilla and a savoury note come in.
Earth and spice take the lead as the intensity climbs, with a creamy, leathery sweetness holding on.

espinosa--laranja-azulejo.description: A Laranja Reserva spin-off made at A.J. Fernández's San Lotano factory in Nicaragua, pairing a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a Brazilian Arapiraca binder and Nicaraguan filler, lightly box-pressed. It is a dense, savoury smoke of pepper, leather and earth, kept in balance by a salty creaminess and some sweetness.

thirds.notes: Black pepper and toasty wood come first; cream softens the smoke after an inch, then leather and a salted nut note appear.
Darker and chewier, with a charred, bittersweet edge; leather returns over pepper and dry earth on the nose.
The pepper sharpens toward chilli flakes, leather and earth dominate, and a touch of citrus shows on the retrohale.

espinosa--laranja-escuro.description: Released in 2019 and made at the San Lotano factory in Ocotal, Nicaragua, this darker Laranja dresses Nicaraguan binder and filler in a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper. It is a rich, dessert-leaning smoke of cocoa, caramel and buttercream, threaded with citrus and pepper, best given time after a meal.

thirds.notes: Pepper leads the first puffs, then fades into buttercream, dark chocolate and a light citrus tang over deepening earth.
Caramel and cocoa build with citrus and earth; sweetness grows and a hotter, spicier finish develops.
Cream and citrus come back together, while pepper can climb and crowd the finer notes near the end.

espinosa--espinosa-crema.description: A gentle blend rolled at La Zona in Estelí with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It keeps to a traditional, creamy path of nuts, wood and gentle pepper, an easy daytime cigar that gathers a little more spice as it burns.

thirds.notes: Walnut and cashew sit in a creamy smoke, with white pepper appearing toward the end of the third.
Light wood and sweet cedar come forward with almond and a soft, creamy texture.
A clove-like spice and deeper pepper join a thicker wood and earthy note, without turning harsh.

espinosa--espinosa-habano.description: Erik Espinosa's first blend from his La Zona factory in Estelí, released in 2012 and reworked with a new band in 2015: a Habano-wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It opens with pepper and coffee, settles into a creamy middle and gathers strength toward a spicy close.

thirds.notes: Light pepper and coffee over cedar, with a hint of citrus in the aroma and a clean, sweet spice.
The smoke turns creamier; coffee grows, cedar sweetens, and a nutty or cocoa note slips in.
Spice and pepper build on the retrohale as the strength rises, over a toasty coffee finish.
